modules/hr/config/hr-document-types.cont: both handlers are @AuthorizedInService with a dual check (hr:documents:view or self:onboarding-docs) because employees need the document-type catalog during onboarding; the hr:documents:manage mutations live in hr-document-types-admin.controller.ts, which is gated
modules/hr/cases/hr-disciplinary.control: HANDOFF: mixes 3 self:cases handlers with 4 hr:cases:view/hr:cases:manage handlers, so a class-level @RequireModule('hr') would take employee self-service away from orgs without an HR subscription. The hr:cases:* handlers need extracting into a gated sibling the way hr-document-types and onboarding-views were. HR lane only — outside this lane's write territory.
modules/hr/onboarding/core/onboarding.co: HANDOFF + REGRESSION: this controller mixes 9 @Universal() self-service handlers, cross-module setup admin (onboarding:module-checklists:*, onboarding:tours:*) and 2 self:onboarding-tasks handlers. Those 2 carried per-method @RequireModule('hr') as of d35ced603 and LOST it in this branch's merge (the diff that added @ResponseSchema also dropped the decorator and its import), so hr onboarding-task reads/writes are now reachable without an HR subscription. Restoring those two decorators is an HR-lane edit — outside this lane's write territory.
modules/crm/import/crm-import.controller: mixes crm:imports:manage handlers, which namespaceOf() already resolves to the plan-gated 'crm' module so authorize() denies them without the subscription, with GET export and GET export/archive, which are deliberately gated on party:parties:view — a non-plan-gated namespace — so that data export does not require an active plan. A class-level @RequireModule('crm') would break that documented portability guarantee.
